newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding via 3-day systems, likely fixed.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding via 3-day systems, likely fixed.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to temporarily add reserves to the banking system on Monday via three-day system repurchase agreements, likely to be fixed, analysts said.

Such operation will complement the outstanding seven-day system repos in place since Thursday and help meet the large daily add need Fed watchers estimate at $4.0 billion through Wednesday, the end of the current reserve maintenance period.
"The seven-day (operation) was not enough to meet the add need. We expect three-day systems, probably fixed," said MCM MoneyWatch senior economist Astrid Adolfson.
The large add need is tied to the traditional rise in currency in circulation during the summer, mainly going into the Labor Day holiday on September 2.
Fixing the repos would give the Fed a guarantee dealers cannot pull out of the operation before it matures, regardless of federal funds rate fluctuations.
Ahead of the 1130 EDT/1530 GMT usual intervention time, federal funds changed hands at 5-1/4 percent, on target.
